concerns.text: Tasks T012a-c (HiLS inference wrapper) and T014a-b (aggregation logic) are listed as implementation tasks for US1, but they depend on the dynamic HiLS model checkpoint and the PG-19 dataset being available. While T004-T006 set up the data loader, there is no explicit task to 'Load/Initialize the pre-trained HiLS checkpoint' before T012 attempts to run inference. The 'Foundational' phase sets up data infrastructure but does not explicitly produce the model artifact required by the US1 implementation tasks, creating a hidden dependency gap.

User Story 2 (Static Index Construction) tasks T019-T022 depend on the output of US1 (`data/interim/relevance_profiles.json`). The task list correctly places US2 after US1, but T019 (PCA reduction) and T020 (K-Means) are marked `[P]` (parallel-safe). This is incorrect: PCA and K-Means cannot run in parallel with each other or with the extraction of profiles if they share the same input file stream without explicit locking or file-based separation. Furthermore, T019 depends on T015 (JSON serialization) completing. Marking T019 as `[P]` implies it can run independently of T015, which violates the producer-consumer flow.

User Story 3 tasks T026-T032 depend on the `static_index.json` produced by US2 (T022). T026 (Static-HiLS inference) is marked `[P]`. This is a violation: T026 cannot run until T022 (serialization of the static index) is complete. The `[P]` tag suggests it can run in parallel with other US3 tasks or even US2 tasks, but it strictly requires the artifact from T022. Additionally, T027 (perplexity calculation) requires both the dynamic baseline (US1) and the static index (US2), making it impossible to run in parallel with T026 if T026 is the only consumer of the index.

Tasks T009 and T010 (Tests for US1) are placed before the implementation tasks (T011-T016). While the 'TDD' note suggests writing tests first, the `[P]` tag on T009/T010 implies they can run in parallel with implementation. However, T009 (Contract test) and T010 (Integration test) depend on the code in T011-T016 to exist to run against. If the intent is 'write the test file first', the `[P]` tag is misleading because the *execution* of these tests is strictly sequential to the implementation. The ordering should reflect that the *files* are created first, but the *tasks* (running tests) must follow implementation.

Tasks T004-T006 (Data Loader, Filtering, Error Handling) are marked `[P]`. While they can be implemented in parallel, T005 (Filtering logic) and T006 (Error handling) logically depend on the structure defined in T004 (Data Loader). If T004 is not complete, T005 and T006 cannot be fully implemented. The `[P]` tag is acceptable for 'implementation' but risky for 'execution' if the pipeline is run as a script. A clearer dependency chain (T004 -> T005 -> T006) or a note that they are parallel-implementation but sequential-execution would be safer.
